filename: Reduced water loss rather than increased photosynthesis controls CO2-enhanced water-use efficiency.pdf
title: Reduced water loss rather than increased photosynthesis controls CO2-enhanced water-use efficiency
code_availability: The code necessary to reproduce the main findings of this study are publicly available via GitHub at https://github.com/Weiwei047/iWUE_CO2.
testbed_rationale: The study develops an offline XGBoost attribution framework to decompose observational flux tower time series and isolate CO2 physiological sensitivity; it does not produce or benchmark an online ML parameterization for climate models.
pain_points: Erroneous long-term sensor trends or calibration drift in eddy covariance CO2 and soil water content (SWC) measurements required replacing in situ data with satellite/reanalysis products (CASM, CAMS, NOAA flasks).
Strong noise and stochasticity at daily resolution necessitate careful signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) filtering to confirm detectable physiological signals.
Collinearity between covarying climatic trends and atmospheric CO2 increases requires differencing and input-perturbation experiments to avoid misattribution.
Sparse geographical coverage of long-term eddy covariance flux towers in tropical regions such as Amazonia and Asia.
extraction_notes: The paper uses ML (XGBoost) as a diagnostic attribution tool rather than as a physical parameterization emulator. It compares observationally derived beta response factors against CMIP6 ESM simulations.
